#### 1. Senior-Loken syndrome 1  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.479)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5620912)

**Proposed mechanism:** NPHP4 (HGNC:28877) —DISRUPTS→ ciliogenesis (GO:0001537); NPHP4 (HGNC:28877) —DISRUPTS→ intraflagellar transport (GO:0031209); NPHP1 (HGNC:7848) —DISRUPTS→ ciliogenesis (GO:0001537); NPHP1 (HGNC:7848) —DISRUPTS→ intraflagellar transport (GO:0031209); ciliogenesis (GO:0001537) —LEADS_TO→ Renal dysfunction (HP:0000094); ciliogenesis (GO:0001537) —LEADS_TO→ Retinal degeneration (HP:0000547); intraflagellar transport (GO:0031209) —LEADS_TO→ Renal dysfunction (HP:0000094); intraflagellar transport (GO:0031209) —LEADS_TO→ Retinal degeneration (HP:0000547). Disruptions in NPHP4 and NPHP1 lead to defects in ciliogenesis and intraflagellar transport, consequently causing renal and retinal dysfunction.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in NPHP4 or NPHP1 that do not impair ciliogenesis or intraflagellar transport would falsify this hypothesis. Alternatively, demonstrating that the disease mechanisms in NPHP4 and NPHP1 converge on entirely distinct cellular pathways unrelated to cilia function would also serve as falsification. _(variant: None specified as causal)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared reliance on ciliary function for both kidney and retinal health could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting ciliogenesis or intraflagellar transport that benefit patients with either nephronophthisis 4 or Senior-Loken syndrome 1.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of NPHP1 and NPHP4 in ciliary function and renal development could lead to therapeutic strategies applicable to both nephronophthisis and Joubert syndrome with renal defect, potentially focusing on restoring ciliary integrity or function.
